prog = '''import json
from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    g = [row[:] for row in grid]
    H, W = len(g), len(g[0])
    bg = Counter(v for row in g for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    # find row bands separated by all-background rows
    bands, cur = [], []
    for i in range(H):
        if any(v != bg for v in g[i]):
            cur.append(i)
        elif cur:
            bands.append((cur[0], cur[-1])); cur = []
    if cur: bands.append((cur[0], cur[-1]))
    if len(bands) < 2:
        return g
    (ra0, ra1), (rb0, rb1) = bands[0], bands[1]
    for i in range(min(ra1 - ra0, rb1 - rb0) + 1):
        ur = max([j for j in range(W) if g[ra0 + i][j] != bg], default=-1)
        lr = max([j for j in range(W) if g[rb0 + i][j] != bg], default=-1)
        for j in range(ur + 1, lr + 1):
            g[ra0 + i][j] = 1
    return g
'''

prog = '''from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    H, W = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    rows = [i for i, r in enumerate(grid) if any(v != bg for v in r)]
    groups = [[rows[0]]]
    for i in rows[1:]:
        if i == groups[-1][-1] + 1:
            groups[-1].append(i)
        else:
            groups.append([i])
    if len(groups) < 2:
        return [r[:] for r in grid]
    rU, rL = groups[0], groups[1]
    bu = [set(j for j, v in enumerate(grid[i]) if v != bg) for i in rU]
    bl = [set(j for j, v in enumerate(grid[i]) if v != bg) for i in rL]
    n = len(bu)
    s = max(range(-10, 11),
            key=lambda s: (sum(len(bu[i] & {j - s for j in bl[i]}) for i in range(n)), -abs(s)))
    out = [r[:] for r in grid]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in bl[i]:
            t = j - s
            if t not in bu[i] and 0 <= t < W:
                out[rU[i]][t] = 1
    return out
'''

def bands(gx, bgc):
    rows = [i for i,r in enumerate(gx) if any(v!=bgc for v in r)]
    # split into contiguous groups
    groups=[]; cur=[rows[0]]
    for i in rows[1:]:
        if i==cur[-1]+1: cur.append(i)
        else: groups.append(cur); cur=[i]
    groups.append(cur)
    return groups
def rowsets(gx, rows):
    return [set(j for j,v in enumerate(gx[i]) if v!=9) for i in rows]
def best_shift(u, l):
    # shift s: l ~= u + s ... try all s, maximize overlap
    best=(0,-1)

import json, os
def transform(grid):
    bgc = grid[0][0]
    gr = bands(grid, bgc)
    A = rsets(grid, gr[0], bgc); B = rsets(grid, gr[1], bgc); W = len(grid[0])
    RU = max(max(r) for r in A); RL = max(max(r) for r in B)
    T = 'U' if RU < RL else 'L'
    tot = {s: sum(len(u & {j - s for j in l}) for u, l in zip(A, B)) for s in range(-W, W + 1)}
    m = max(tot.values()); s = min([x for x in tot if tot[x] == m], key=abs)
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for i, (u, l) in enumerate(zip(A, B)):
        if T == 'U':
            add = {c - s for c in l if (c - s) > max(u)}
            ri = gr[0][i]
        else:
            add = {c + s for c in u if (c + s) > max(l)}
            ri = gr[1][i]
        for p in add:
            if 0 <= p < W:
                out[ri][p] = 1
    return out

def solve_h(gi, bg):
    H, W = len(gi), len(gi[0])
    (ra, A), (rb, B) = bands_of(gi, bg)
    RUA = max(max(s) for s in A); RUB = max(max(s) for s in B)
    T, D, rt = (B, A, rb) if RUB < RUA else (A, B, ra)
    best_s, best_v = 0, -1
    for s in range(-(W-1), W):
        tot = sum(len(t & {c+s for c in d}) for t, d in zip(T, D))
        if tot > best_v: best_v, best_s = tot, s
    s = best_s
    out = [row[:] for row in gi]
    for i, (t, d) in enumerate(zip(T, D)):
        matched = {c+s for c in d} & t
        if not matched: continue
        k = max(matched)  # last matched target position = cut
        for c in d:
            cc = c + s
            if cc > k and 0 <= cc < W:
                out[rt[0]+i][cc] = 1
    return out, s

for name, gi, go, bg in demos5:
    pred, s = solve_h(gi, bg)
    print(name, 's=%d' % s, 'MATCH' if pred == go else 'DIFF')

That means bands_of picked different rows? The test lower band rows 20–26: row 20 = "9 9 9 9 9 9 9 8 9 9 9 9 8 9 8 8 8 9 9 9 8 8 9 8 9 8 9 9 9" → cells {7,12,15,16,17,21,22,24,26}. Yes! The summary's rowsets were wrong (probably from an older mis-parse!). Current: l0 = {7,12,15,16,17,21,22,24,26}. Let me recompute: row20 string: index: 0-6 are 9, 7 is 8, 8-11 9, 12 8, 13-14 9, 15 8,16 8,17 8, 18-20 9, 21 8,22 8, 23 9, 24 8, 25 9,26 8. So {7,12,15,16,17,21,22,24,26} ✓ matches bands_of.

Hmm! So my earlier "noise at 24,26" analysis used a WRONG l0! Let me redo the whole test analysis with the correct data. Upper row0: "9 9 9 9 9 8 9 9 9 9 8 9 8 8 8 9 9 9 8 8 9 8 9 8 9 9 8 9 9": {5,10,12,13,14,18,19,21,23,26} ✓.

So row0: u+2 = {7,12,14,15,16,20,21,23,25,28}; l = {8,13,15,16,17,21,22,24,26}: matched = {15,16,21} only! ov=3. t-extras = {8,13,17,22,24,26}, u-extras = {5,10,12,18,21?} wait 21 ∈ u: 21+2=23 ∉ l → u-extras include 21? printed: [5,10,12,18,21,23,26]... and 19? 19+2=21 ∈ l ✓ matched. OK.

This is a VERY noisy row — ov only 3. So maybe row0's true shift isn't 2?! And the global s=2 was driven by other rows. Rows 2,3 exact truncation at s=2 — solid. Row1: u+2 ⊂ l with extra {0}: l = (u+2) ∪ {0}: truncation with ONE extra noise at 0... wait extra at 0 is BEFORE. l = {0} ∪ (u+2)! exact except prepended noise. row4: l = {1} ∪ u+2, extra at 1. row6: l = {1} ∪ (u+2 ∩...): matched {3,5,13,14,15,18,21,22,24}, u-extras {25,28}: l = {1} ∪ matched.

So per-row structure: rows 1,4,6: target = donor+2 cut, plus one noise cell near left (0 or 1). Row 2,3: pure truncations. Row 5: exact truncation. Row 0: heavily noisy — maybe row 0's true relationship: is l0 = (u0+s) cut for some other s? Check s values for row0 alone: u0 = {5,10,12,13,14,18,19,21,23,26}. Try s=3: u0+3 = {8,13,15,16,17,21,22,24,26,29}: l0 = {8,13,15,16,17,21,22,24,26}: l0 = (u0+3) ∩ ≤26 EXACTLY!!! l0 is a perfect truncation of u0+3! So ROW 0 has shift s=3, not 2!!

So per-row shifts differ: row0: s=3; rows1-6: s=2. But wait — global shift should be rigid... unless the donor pattern for row0 differs. Actually maybe the upper band's row0 is a different pattern row... whatever — empirically row0 aligns perfectly at s=3 (9 of 9 cells), v8 (per-row ov argmax with tie min|s|) computed row0 argmax ov... earlier v8 said row0 s=3 gave painted... wait v8 was per-row argmax ov: row0: ov at s=2 = 3; at s=3 = 9! So per-row argmax = s=3 → painted = {c+3 > max(l0)=26} = {c=26 → 29 out} → nothing?? Hmm: c+3 > 26 → c ≥ 24: c=26 → 29 out of grid → row0 paints NOTHING at cut=26! But v8's output included B,C,D,E,F (rows 1-6) and no row0 cell — v8 = {B,C,D,E,F} rejected! Hmm!!

Wait, v8 rejected. So v8 (row0: nothing, others standard paints) is wrong. But now rows 1-6: v8's per-row shifts: row1: ov at s=2 = 7 (matched 7 of 8) — is s=2 the argmax? s=0: matched = l∩u = {0,2}? Let me just trust v8's earlier calc: row1 → s=2 painted {c+2 > 22}: u1 max 20 → 22 not > 22 → nothing. rows 2,3,5,6 → B,C,D,E,F. So v8 = {B,C,D,E,F} rejected.

So truth differs from {B,C,D,E,F} somewhere: either row0 (with s=3, cut could be < 26 if noise... but row0 is a PERFECT truncation at s=3, so cut = 26, nothing beyond, except... c=26+3=29 out of bounds) or rows 1-6 need different cut/paint.

Hmm wait — maybe at s=3, row0's cut: l0 = (u0+3) truncated: max = 26; donor cells beyond: 29 out. So nothing. Consistent with v8's row0.

So the difference must be in rows 1-6 painting. B=(22,27), C=(23,27), D=(23,28), E=(25,26), F=(26,27). One or more of these wrong, or missing cells.

Reconsider per-row cut: for rows 1,4,6, target has a noise cell at the LEFT (0 or 1). Interesting — noise at left. For row1: l1 = {0} ∪ (u1+2). Perfect. Row4: l4 = {1} ∪ u4+2 exact. Row6: l6 = {1} ∪ matched where u-extras {25,28} unmatched — noise in donor? or... l6 = {1,3,5,13,14,15,18,21,22,24}: u6+2 = {3,5,13,14,15,18,21,22,24,27,30}: matched 9, u-extras 25,28 → these would paint {27} if cut=24. 

Hmm, what if the noise at left (cells 0/1) means the DONOR is actually cut on the left... no.

Alternatively, maybe the true relationship is that the donor (upper) band itself is a shifted+truncated version of the SAME pattern as target but to the LEFT: pattern P_i: u_i = (P_i) truncated right at some k_u; l_i = (P_i + s_i) truncated at k_l. Painting fills l_i's tail from P_i + s_i.

If rows have DIFFERENT shifts (row0: 3, others: 2), maybe there's no global rigidity — the two copies might each be shifted differently per row?! That seems odd but the data says row0: 3.

Hmm wait, actually maybe row0's upper is NOISY and the true shift is 2 with more noise... l0 vs u0+2: matched {15,16,21} only — 6 extras. Too many. s=3 exact. So per-row shifts: row0: 3, rows 1-6: 2.

Now with per-row shifts, cut = max(target) per row (v8's method with per-row argmax ov). v8 rejected. With (h)-style per-row: k = last matched: row1: last matched 22 → nothing; same as v8 for all rows except... rows 2,3,5,6: max(target) matched → same. So per-row variants ≡ v8. Rejected!

So {B,C,D,E,F} is wrong. Which cells? Maybe the truth paints cells in row0 after all: with s=3, cut... l0 = u0+3 truncated at 26: painted = cells of u0+3 beyond cut: 29 — out of grid. Nothing. Unless painted condition uses donor frame: c > max(l0)−3 = 23: c ∈ u0, c > 23: {26} → 29 out. Nothing.

Hmm, so row0 contributes nothing under both. Then truth ⊆ rows1-6 cells ⊆ {12?...}: candidates beyond cut: row1: c+2 > 22: none (u1 max 20). row2: {27}. row3: {27,28}. row4: none. row5: {26}. row6: {27}. That's exactly v8! Rejected!! Contradiction — meaning the CUT for some rows must be LOWER than max(target), or painting isn't "beyond cut".

Wait... unless painted cells can also fill INTERIOR gaps?! Rows 1,4,6 have noise at left; row0 very noisy. But row2: l2 = {11,14,19,24} ⊆ u2+2 with u-extras {25,28}: what if the target noise... there's none in row2. Hmm.

OR: maybe painted = fill from cut to END OF PATTERN where pattern extends beyond the grid... no.

Let me recheck: maybe the shift for some rows isn't 2 either! Check each row for exact truncation across shifts (donor s such that target ⊆ donor+s, target-extras = 0):
row1: l1 ⊆ u1+s: s=2: l1∖(u1+2) = {0} ✗. Other s? u1 = {0,2,7,10,14,15,20}: try s=2 gives best. s=? l1 = {0,2,4,9,12,16,17,22}: u1−?: hmm target might extend beyond donor. Only subset direction matters. Probably s=2 with 1 noise.
row4: {1} extra. s=2.
row6: {1} extra, s=2.
row5: exact s=2.
rows2,3: exact s=2.
row0: exact s=3.

So all rows s=2 except row0 s=3. Under cut=max(target): paints = v8 = rejected. Under any sensible cut estimator rows 2,3,5 are pure: cut = max, paints B,{C,D},E. Row6: {F}. So {B,C,D,E,F} ⊆ truth presumably, PLUS something extra that v8 lacked. v8 lacked row0 paints. With row0 s=3: donor u0 beyond cut 26: {29} out of grid. BUT what if painted cells outside the grid WRAP or get clamped?? c=26+3=29 → W−1=28?? → (20,28) = A! v5 = v8 ∪ {A} rejected though! Hmm, v5 = A,B,C,D,E,F rejected. So truth = {B,C,D,E,F} ∪ X where X ∉ {{}, {A}}.

X possibilities: row0 cells from s=3 donor beyond cut if cut < 26 — but row0's target is exact, cut = 26. What if painted = {c+s > max(target) − 1}? i.e., ≥? row2: 24 not ≥ 25... no.

What if X comes from row0 painting based on s=2 alignment?? ugh.

What if X = {(21,22)}? row1: u1 = {...,20}: 20+2 = 22 = max(l1) already there.

Hmm what if some rows' donor extends and painting includes 29→ beyond grid gets CLIPPED but... nothing.

Let me reconsider: maybe T = UPPER band this time?! Global max: upper row3 max 28 > lower row3 max 25 → T = lower by smaller-max. But wait, with row0 having shift 3 and exact truncation... hmm. What if T is the band with more EXACT rows? Both same...

Actually, WAIT. What if I have the direction wrong: what if the UPPER band is the truncated one and painting fills the UPPER band's tail?! Check: is upper = lower+s truncated anywhere? Row2: u2 = {9,12,17,22,25,28}: l2−2 = {9,12,17,22}: u2 = (l2−2) ∪ {25,28}: upper extends BEYOND lower by {25,28}: so upper could be the FULL pattern and lower truncated — that's our assumption (donor=upper). Alternatively upper = (l2−2) ∪ {25,28}: the extras could be upper's own... upper is the donor (full). Right.

But hmm, what if the UPPER band is truncated and the LOWER is the full pattern? Then u2 would need ⊆ l2−2: {25,28} ∉ ✗. Unless noise. Row2: u2∖(l2−2) = {25,28} = 2 extras. Upper-as-target: s: u ⊆ l+s': l2−2 ⊆ u2 with extras... try s'=−2: covered. Generally T=lower fits better.

OK here's another thought: what if painted cells get color 1 but ALSO existing unmatched noise cells in target beyond... no.

Let me step back and think about v8's rejection differently. Maybe the per-row ov-argmax for some row differs from what v8 computed. v8: per-row shift = argmax ov, tie min|s|. Row0: ov(s=3)=9 > ov(s=2)=3 → s=3 → nothing painted. But what if tie-break/global constraint forces s=2 for row0 too (global rigidity), and then row0's cut = 26: painted = {c+2 > 26} = {28} = A. v5 rejected. OR cut = last-matched at s=2: matched {15,16,21}: k=21: painted = {c+2 > 21} = {23,25,28}: that's (h)-row0 — also rejected.

Hmm, everything obvious is rejected. What remains? Maybe painting with s=3 for row0 but cut relative to... let me enumerate what cells row0 could paint under s=3: {c+3 > k}: k=26 → ∅; k=21? no basis. 

Maybe the answer: painted = {c+s_i: c ∈ u_i, c+s_i > max(l_i)} per-row with per-row shift — v8 — rejected. 

Hmm, wait, maybe I should double-check v8's actual computation — the summary says v8 = v5 − {(20,28)}, but with row0 at s=3 v8 should paint nothing in row0 — consistent (no (20,28)) ✓.

So both "no row0 paint" and three row0-paint variants rejected. Therefore truth must differ in rows 1-6 from {B,C,D,E,F}!! Either additional cells or different cells. Additional cells must come from donor cells beyond cut... rows 1,4: none. Unless cut < max(target) for those rows: rows 1,4,6 have noise at LEFT (cell 0/1). What if the noise is at the left because... OH WAIT. What if the truncation is on the LEFT, not the right?! What if the target is shifted RIGHT and truncated on the LEFT, and painted cells fill the LEFT?! Let me check: D1: painted cols 11-12 (right side). Hmm right side.

But wait — rows 1,4,6 test: target = {0 or 1} ∪ (u+2): the {0}/{1} cell is EXTRA at the left. If instead the target were u+2 shifted RIGHT by 1 relative to... l1 = {0,2,4,9,12,16,17,22}: u1+1 = {1,3,8,11,15,16,21}: no. It's just noise.

Alternatively — maybe those left cells indicate that the donor row itself starts differently... 

Hmm, let me look at D3's noise positions: D3 row1: l1 = {0..9,11,14}, u1+2 = {2..9,11,14}: extras {0,1} at LEFT. D3 row0: extras {1} left. D4: noise = extra cells {26,27} at RIGHT end of target (l0 = u0 ∪ {26,27}) — painted over? no wait: D4: T=U, target u0, donor l0 = u0 ∪ {26,27}: donor extras at right {26,27} → PAINTED (1,26),(1,27)! So in D4, the "noise" cells {26,27} in the DONOR at the right end are exactly the painted cells! The donor is full pattern, u0 is the truncation, and painting = donor beyond cut. ✓ consistent.

In test row6: u-extras {25,28} → paint {27}: c=28 → 30 OUT OF GRID. c=25 → 27 ✓ F. Row5: u-extras {24,27} → 26 ✓ E, 29 out. Row2: {25,28} → 27 ✓ B, 30 out. Row3: {25,26,28} → 27,28 ✓ C,D, 30 out.

So out-of-grid sources: 26→29 (row0 s=3), 27→29 (row5), 28→30 (rows 2,3,6). All beyond W−1=28. Clipping = dropping is natural. But what if instead the pattern/grid conceptually EXTENDS: painted cells beyond the grid are lost. Fine.

So candidate truth sets: {B,C,D,E,F} (v8, REJ), plus-A (v5, REJ), plus {(20,23),(20,25),(20,28)} (h — but wait, (h) used the WRONG l0! (h) was computed with old wrong rowsets? No — solve_h used bands_of which gives correct rowsets; (h) test pred = {(20,23),(20,25),(20,28),...}: that used s=2 global with last-matched k. With correct data, row0's matched at s=2 = {15,16,21}: k=21: painted = c+2>21: {23,25,28} ✓ that's what it did. Rejected.)

Remaining possibilities: truth = {B,C,D,E,F} ∪ row0 cells where row0 uses s=3 with cut < 26?? row0 target is EXACT at s=3 — no noise, so cut = 26 definitively. Painting beyond → only 29 (out). So row0 = ∅. Then truth = {B,C,D,E,F} = v8. REJECTED. Contradiction!!!

Unless... one of B,C,D,E,F is wrong! Which could be wrong? They all come from exact-truncation rows with clean cut = max(target). Row5: l5 = u5+2 truncated exactly at 22, donor extras {24,27} → paint {26}. Certain. Row2: {27}. Certain. Row3: {27,28}. Certain. Row6: {27} — l6 = {1} ∪ (u6+2 ∩...): l6∖(u6+2) = {1}: so l6 = u6+2 truncated at 24 plus noise {1}: cut = 24: paint {27}. Certain-ish.

Row1: l1 = {0} ∪ (u1+2) exactly: cut 22: paint ∅. Certain-ish.

So truth should = v8. But v8 rejected! Unless the submission format/grid had an issue, or bands_of rows differ from what I think... OR the output requires REMOVING noise too!! Maybe the output also cleans the target: e.g., removes the noise cells ({0}, {1}, ...) or re-colors noise?? In demos, pred==go with add-only... but maybe demo noise cells coincided with positions that are pattern cells... D3 row1 extras {0,1}: output kept them 8? pred==go means output = input + paints. If the true rule also removed noise, demo outputs would differ... unless demo noise wasn't noise but pattern? Hmm wait — D3 row1 extras {0,1} at left: what if they're NOT noise but part of pattern shifted... l1 = {0..9,11,14}: if s=2, matched = {2..9,11,14}: extras {0,1}: alternatively s such that more matches: no.

Hold on, let me re-examine: maybe the shift per row is such that target ⊆ donor+s with ZERO extras for ALL rows, and my "extras" are actually donor noise... no — extras are in TARGET, unmatched. Rows 1,4,6 each have exactly 1 extra at 0 or 1, row0 (at s=2) 6 extras but s=3 exact.

Hmm interesting pattern: extras at columns 0,1,1 in rows 1,4,6. And row0 perfect at s=3. What if actually the pattern rows themselves are: the lower band = upper band rows REORDERED?? No...

What if the upper band rows are the lower rows shifted by −s AND the noise is in the UPPER: i.e., true pattern P: l_i = P_i + 2 truncated... u_i = P_i ∪ noise or P_i minus noise? Row0: if s=3: l0 = u0+3 truncated exactly: so u0 ⊇ pattern−3: u0 = P0−3 possibly + noise. Painting = l0 tail beyond 26: nothing. Row1: l1 = u1+2 ∪ {0}: u1 ⊆ P−2? l1's 0 is extra → in target = noise.

Alternatively! What if extras at 0/1 in target rows 1,4,6 and row0's perfect s=3 hint at ROW SHIFTS: the lower band might be shifted by a DIFFERENT amount per row because the "shift" isn't translation but... hmm, actually what if the shift direction relates to the row: maybe the transform shifts each row by s_i where s_i varies (like a shear)? Rows 1-6: s=2, row0: s=3?? If s_i = 2 + (i==0)? Bizarre.

OR the upper band rows might be shifted per-row: upper = pattern truncated, with row0 shifted...

But maybe row0's pattern row just happens to be shift-ambiguous? At s=2 only 3 match — no.

Hmm OK, so what if the transform = shift by s per row = global 2 EXCEPT the shift applies to the pattern P, and row0's upper copy is at pattern−3 while others at pattern−2?? i.e., the upper band itself is internally inconsistent = the upper band has per-row noise in the SHIFT?? Weird.

Alternative: maybe I misidentified which rows pair up! Maybe the bands pair differently: e.g., upper row i pairs with lower row (i+1) or similar! If lower row 0 pairs with upper row... let me check: lower row0 = {8,13,15,16,17,21,22,24,26} matched upper row0 at s=3 exactly. Other rows matched at s=2 with same index. What if row0 of lower actually derives from a DIFFERENT upper row (not row0)? Under global s=2: which upper row, shifted by 2, truncated, gives l0 = {8,13,15,16,17,21,22,24,26}? Need upper row r with {8,13,15,16,17,21,22,24,26} ⊆ u_r+2 = u_r+{2}: u_r ⊇ {6,11,13,14,15,19,20,22,24}: no upper row has these (u0 = {5,10,12,13,14,18,19,21,23,26} — no). So pairing is same-index.

OK here's another thought — maybe the OUTPUT fills the tail with 1s from the cut to the DONOR's max extent... same thing.

Let me now consider that maybe the cut for painting is the DONOR's... hmm.

What if painted = {c+s: c+s > max(target)} where per-row s from argmax ov BUT for row0, argmax ov at s=3... nothing. So v8 again.

Everything points to v8. It's rejected. So some structural assumption is off. What if painted color isn't 1 in all cases... demos show 1. What if output also paints in the UPPER band when the upper is the truncated one... here upper is donor.

What if the OUTPUT for the test differs in rows OUTSIDE the bands? No.

Let me recheck the rejection list: is it possible v8's submitted grid had an error (e.g., wrong bg or a stray cell)? The summary says v8 submitted = v5 minus (20,28) — computed by tr. Trust it.

Hmm, let me look at the LEFT noise cells again: rows 1,4,6 have extra cells at columns 0,1,1. Rows 2,3,5 have NO extras. Row0 (s=3) none. Check D1/D3: D3 row1: extras {0,1} — if those were left-truncation evidence... no wait, extras = cells present that shouldn't be — that's the opposite.

Alternatively, maybe rows 1,4,6's {0}/{1} cells mean the lower band rows are SHIFTED LEFT by... l1 = u1+2 ∪ {0}: hmm what if instead l1 = (u1 ∪ {−2}) + 2? = u1+2 ∪ {0} where −2 ∈ u1's pattern but donor truncated left at 0! Then painted = {c+2: c ∈ P−2, c+2 > k} — the donor's missing left cells don't affect right painting. No help.

Let me try assuming noise can appear anywhere and the cut k_i = max(l_i) always (v5's v12 with global s=2) — rejected (v5). Per-row s (v8) — rejected. Last-matched (h, global s=2) — rejected. Per-row last-matched ≡ v8 (except row0: at s=3, matched = all, k = 26: nothing — same as v8). So per-row-h ≡ v8. Rejected.

What produces DIFFERENT cells? Ideas:
1. Paint using donor row's cells c+s > max(target) where donor = the FULL row = union of both copies' info: P_i = (u_i ∪ (l_i − s_i)) minus noise. Row3: P = u3 ∪ (l3−2) = u3 (l3−2 ⊆ u3? l3−2 = {6,9,12,13,15,18,19,20,22,23} ⊆ u3 ✓). Same → no change.

Let me try to actually reconstruct the underlying pattern rows and see which extras are noise. Consider that BOTH copies may be noisy. Pattern P_i must satisfy: u_i ⊆ P_i, l_i − s ⊆ P_i. def solve_T(gi, go=None, bgc=None):
    H, Wd = len(gi), len(gi[0])
    # find shape color (not bg, not 1)
    cnt = {}
    for row in gi:
        for v in row: cnt[v]=cnt.get(v,0)+1
    bgc = max(cnt, key=cnt.get)
    fg = [c for c in cnt if c not in (bgc,1)]
    fg = fg[0] if fg else 8
    bandrows = [i for i in range(H) if any(v==fg for v in gi[i])]
    # split into two contiguous groups
    grps=[[bandrows[0]]]
    for i in bandrows[1:]:
        if i == grps[-1][-1]+1: grps[-1].append(i)
        else: grps.append([i])
    g1, g2 = grps
    def cells(grp): return {(i,j) for i in grp for j in range(Wd) if gi[i][j]==fg}
    c1, c2 = cells(g1), cells(g2)
    m1 = max(j for _,j in c1); m2 = max(j for _,j in c2)
    small, big = (g1,g2) if m1 < m2 else (g2,g1)
    cut = min(m1,m2)
    out = [row[:] for row in gi]
    off = small[0]-big[0]
    for (i,j) in cells(big):
        if j > cut:
            r = i+off
            out[r][j] = 1
    return out

ok = True

    good = p==go
    ok &= good
    print(name, good)

import json,itertools
G=json.load(open('/tmp/G.json'))
def bands(g):
    H=len(g); W=len(g[0]); bg=max(itertools.chain(*g), key=[v for r in g for v in r].count)
    rows=[r for r in range(H) if any(v!=bg for v in g[r])]
    bs=[];cur=[rows[0]]
    for r in rows[1:]:
        if r==cur[-1]+1: cur.append(r)
        else: bs.append(cur); cur=[r]
    bs.append(cur)
    return bs,bg
for name in sorted(G):
    if name.startswith('Demo') and 'input' in name:
        g=G[name]; o=G[name.replace('input','output')]
        bs,bg=bands(g)
        print('==',name,'bg',bg,'bands',bs)
        A,B=bs[0],bs[1]
        ch=[(i,j,g[i][j],o[i][j]) for i in range(len(g)) for j in range(len(g[0])) if g[i][j]!=o[i][j]]
        print(' changed rows', sorted(set(i for i,_,_,_ in ch)), 'cols', sorted(set(j for _,j,_,_ in ch)))
        # compare each A row to each B row: best shift
        for i,(ra,rb) in enumerate(zip(A,B)):
            ua=[j for j,v in enumerate(g[ra]) if v!=bg]; ub=[j for j,v in enumerate(g[rb]) if v!=bg]
            best=max(range(-20,21), key=lambda s: len(set(j for j in ua)&set(j-s for j in ub)))
            print('  rowpair',i,'Aext',ua[-1] if ua else None,'Bext',ub[-1] if ub else None,'bestshift',best,'overlap',len(set(ua)&set(j-best for j in ub)))

def solve(gin):
    n=len(gin); W=len(gin[0])
    from collections import Counter
    cnt=Counter(v for r in gin for v in r)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # bands: contiguous runs of rows containing fg
    fgrows=[any(v!=bg for v in r) for r in gin]
    bands=[]; cur=None
    for i,f in enumerate(fgrows):
        if f:
            if cur is None: cur=[i,i]
            else: cur[1]=i
        else:
            if cur is not None: bands.append(tuple(cur)); cur=None
    if cur is not None: bands.append(tuple(cur))
    assert len(bands)==2, bands
    (a0,a1),(b0,b1)=bands
    Arows=gin[a0:a1+1]; Brows=gin[b0:b1+1]
    assert len(Arows)==len(Brows)
    def exts(rows): return [max(c for c,v in enumerate(r) if v!=bg) for r in rows]
    ea=exts(Arows); eb=exts(Brows)
    S,L,dS,dL=(Arows,Brows,ea,eb) if max(ea)<=max(eb) else (Brows,Arows,eb,ea)
    extS0=exts(S)[0]; extL0=exts(L)[0]
    # shift d: maximize |S0 fg ∩ (L0 fg + d)|, tie-break smallest |d| then positive
    s0={c for c,v in enumerate(S[0]) if v!=bg}
    l0={c for c,v in enumerate(L[0]) if v!=bg}
    def ov(d): return len(s0 & {c+d for c in l0})
    best=max(range(-W,W), key=lambda d:(ov(d), -abs(d), d))
    d=best
    theta=min(exts(S))+1
    out=[row[:] for row in gin]
    changed=[]
    for i in range(len(S)):
        for c in range(theta, W):
            if S[i][c]==bg and (c-d) in lset[i] if False else (S[i][c]==bg and (c-d)>=0 and (c-d)<W and L[i][c-d]!=bg):
                out[a0+i if S is Arows else b0+i][c]=1
                changed.append((i,c))
    return out, dict(bg=bg,d=d,theta=theta,S='A' if S is Arows else 'B',changed=changed, lset=None)

ok=True
for k in range(1,9):
    gin=G[f'Demo {k} input']; gexp=G[f'Demo {k} output']
    out,info=solve(gin)
    good = out==gexp
    ok &= good
    print(k, 'OK' if good else 'FAIL', info['bg'], 'd=',info['d'], 'theta=',info['theta'], 'S=',info['S'], 'nchanged=',len(info['changed']))
print('ALL', ok)

from collections import Counter

def solve(gin, verbose=False):
    n=len(gin); W=len(gin[0])
    cnt=Counter(v for r in gin for v in r)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    fgrows=[any(v!=bg for v in r) for r in gin]
    bands=[];cur=None
    for i,f in enumerate(fgrows):
        if f: cur=[i,i] if cur is None else [cur[0],i]
        else:
            if cur: bands.append(tuple(cur)); cur=None
    if cur: bands.append(tuple(cur))
    assert len(bands)==2, bands
    (a0,a1),(b0,b1)=bands
    A=gin[a0:a1+1]; B=gin[b0:b1+1]
    assert len(A)==len(B)
    exts=lambda rows:[max(c for c,v in enumerate(r) if v!=bg) for r in rows]
    ea,eb=exts(A),exts(B)
    S,L,sA=(A,B) if max(ea)<=max(eb) else (B,A)
    eS,eL=exts(S),exts(L)
    R=min(eS[0],eL[0])
    s0=[c for c,v in enumerate(S[0]) if v!=bg]
    l0=[c for c,v in enumerate(L[0]) if v!=bg]
    def ovf(s):
        return sum(1 for c in s0 if c<=R and 0<=c+s<W and L[0][c+s]!=bg)
    best=None
    for s in range(-W+1,W):
        key=(ovf(s), -abs(s), -s)
        if best is None or key>best[0]: best=(key,s)
    s=best[1]
    theta=min(eS)+1
    out=[r[:] for r in gin]
    ch=[]
    off = a0 if S is A else b0
    for i in range(len(S)):
        for c in range(theta,W):
            if S[i][c]==bg and 0<=c+s<W and L[i][c+s]!=bg:
                out[off+i][c]=1; ch.append((off+i,c))
    if verbose: print('bg',bg,'s',s,'theta',theta,'S is A',S is A,'nch',len(ch),ch)
    return out

ok=all(solve(G[f'Demo pair {k} input'])==G[f'Demo pair {k} output'] for k in range(1,9))
print('ALL 8 DEMOS:', ok)

def solve(gin, verbose=False):
    W=len(gin[0])
    cnt=Counter(v for r in gin for v in r)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    fgrows=[any(v!=bg for v in r) for r in gin]
    bands=[];cur=None
    for i,f in enumerate(fgrows):
        if f: cur=[i,i] if cur is None else [cur[0],i]
        else:
            if cur: bands.append(tuple(cur)); cur=None
    if cur: bands.append(tuple(cur))
    (a0,a1),(b0,b1)=bands
    A=gin[a0:a1+1]; B=gin[b0:b1+1]
    exts=lambda rows:[max(c for c,v in enumerate(r) if v!=bg) for r in rows]
    ea,eb=exts(A),exts(B)
    S,L=(A,B) if max(ea)<=max(eb) else (B,A)
    eS,eL=exts(S),exts(L)
    R=eS[0]
    s0=[c for c,v in enumerate(S[0]) if v!=bg]
    ovf=lambda s: sum(1 for c in s0 if c<=R and 0<=c+s<W and L[0][c+s]!=bg)
    s=max(((ovf(s),-abs(s),-s),s) for s in range(-W+1,W))[1]
    theta=min(eS)+1
    out=[r[:] for r in gin]; ch=[]
    off = a0 if S is A else b0
    for i in range(len(S)):
        for c in range(theta,W):
            if S[i][c]==bg and 0<=c+s<W and L[i][c+s]!=bg:
                out[off+i][c]=1; ch.append((off+i,c))
    if verbose: print('bg',bg,'s',s,'theta',theta,'S=A',S is A,'ch',ch)
    return out

prog='''from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    W = len(grid[0])
    cnt = Counter(v for r in grid for v in r)
    bg = cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    fgrows = [any(v != bg for v in r) for r in grid]
    bands = []; cur = None
    for i, f in enumerate(fgrows):
        if f:
            cur = [i, i] if cur is None else [cur[0], i]
        else:
            if cur: bands.append(tuple(cur)); cur = None
    if cur: bands.append(tuple(cur))
    (a0, a1), (b0, b1) = bands
    A = grid[a0:a1+1]; B = grid[b0:b1+1]
    exts = lambda rows: [max(c for c, v in enumerate(r) if v != bg) for r in rows]
    ea, eb = exts(A), exts(B)
    S, L = (A, B) if max(ea) <= max(eb) else (B, A)
    eS, eL = exts(S), exts(L)
    R = min(eS[0], eL[0])
    def ovf(s):
        t = 0
        for i in range(len(S)):
            t += sum(1 for c in range(R+1) if 0 <= c+s <= R and S[i][c] != bg and L[i][c+s] != bg)
        return t
    s = max(((ovf(s), -abs(s), -s), s) for s in range(-W+1, W))[1]
    theta = min(eS) + 1
    out = [r[:] for r in grid]
    off = a0 if S is A else b0
    for i in range(len(S)):
        for c in range(theta, W):
            if S[i][c] == bg and 0 <= c+s < W and L[i][c+s] != bg:
                out[off+i][c] = 1
    return out
'''
